metadata.name: Personal Development Memory
metadata.description: Simulated developer activity over 3 months - conversations with AI coding assistants, git commits, code reviews, configuration changes. Tests understanding of coding philosophy, style patterns, and problem-solving approaches.

learners.name: Generic Developer Memory
learners.purpose: Understand core development philosophy, coding style patterns, and recurring problem-solving approaches

learners.name: Philosophy Specialist
learners.purpose: Understand the developer's core beliefs about software engineering - what they value, what they avoid, and why

learners.name: Code Style Specialist
learners.purpose: Track coding style patterns - naming conventions, formatting preferences, structural choices, and code organization

learners.name: Tooling Specialist
learners.purpose: Understand tool preferences - libraries, frameworks, testing tools, linters, and development environment choices

queries: What testing practices do I follow?
Do I prefer OOP or functional?
What are my thoughts on abstractions?
How do I approach code reviews?

events.content:
[Context: Starting new project]

I'm starting a new API project. Should I use NestJS or just plain Express?

[Assistant]: For a new API, both are valid choices...

[User]: I think I'll go with plain Express. NestJS feels over-engineered for what I need. I can add structure as I go.

chore: init project with minimal express setup
Files: src/index.ts, package.json, tsconfig.json
+45 -0

[Context: Project structure]

What folder structure do you recommend?

[Assistant]: Common patterns include feature-based, layer-based...

[User]: I'll start flat and extract when patterns emerge. Premature structure is as bad as premature optimization.

feat: add user registration endpoint
Files: src/routes/users.ts, src/handlers/register.ts
+89 -0

PR: PR #12 - Add logging middleware [reject]
This abstracts too early. We only have 3 routes. Just add console.log where needed and extract a middleware when we have 10+ routes.

[Context: Error handling]

How should I handle errors in Express routes?

[Assistant]: You can use try/catch, error middleware, or Result types...

[User]: I'll use explicit returns. throw feels like goto. If a function can fail, I want it in the return type.

feat: add Result type for explicit error handling
Files: src/types/result.ts
+34 -0

File: tsconfig.json
Change: Set strict: true, noImplicitAny: true, strictNullChecks: true
Reason: Type safety is non-negotiable

[Context: Validation]

What's the best validation library?

[Assistant]: Popular options include Joi, Yup, Zod...

[User]: Zod looks good. TypeScript-first, infers types automatically. One source of truth for runtime and compile-time validation.

zod@^3.22.0
Reason: Schema validation with type inference

refactor: use zod schemas for request validation
Files: src/schemas/user.ts, src/handlers/register.ts
+56 -23

[Context: Testing strategy]

Should I write unit tests or integration tests first?

[Assistant]: Testing pyramid suggests unit tests at base...

[User]: I'll focus on integration tests for APIs. Unit tests for pure functions only. Testing implementation details is a waste of time.

test: add integration tests for user registration
Files: tests/integration/register.test.ts
+78 -0

PR: PR #15 - Add UserService class [reject]
Why a class? This has no state. Just export functions. Classes should only exist when you need encapsulated state.

[Context: Database choice]

Postgres or MongoDB for this project?

[Assistant]: Depends on your data model...

[User]: Postgres. Relational data, ACID transactions, and I actually know my schema. NoSQL is for when you don't know your data model yet.

feat: add postgres connection with raw SQL
Files: src/db/connection.ts, src/db/queries/users.ts
+67 -0

[Context: ORM choice]

Should I use Prisma or TypeORM?

[Assistant]: Both are popular choices...

[User]: Neither for now. Raw SQL with a thin wrapper. ORMs add magic I don't need yet. If queries get complex, I'll add Kysely.

PR: PR #18 - Add repository pattern [reject]
Repository pattern for 2 tables? This is enterprise cosplay. Just use the query functions directly.

refactor: simplify db layer, remove unnecessary abstractions
Files: src/db/queries/users.ts
+12 -45

[Context: Naming conventions]

camelCase or snake_case for API responses?

[Assistant]: JavaScript convention is camelCase, but some prefer snake_case for APIs...

[User]: camelCase everywhere. One convention, no translation layers. The API is consumed by JS clients anyway.

feat: add authentication with JWT
Files: src/auth/jwt.ts, src/middleware/auth.ts
+89 -0

[Context: JWT storage]

Where should I store JWT tokens on the client?

[Assistant]: Options include localStorage, sessionStorage, httpOnly cookies...

[User]: httpOnly cookies. Never trust client-side storage with auth tokens. XSS is too easy.

File: .prettierrc
Change: Set printWidth: 100, useTabs: true, singleQuote: true
Reason: Tabs for accessibility, single quotes for consistency

PR: PR #22 - Add comments to all functions [reject]
These comments just repeat the function name. 'getUserById gets a user by ID' - I can read. Remove noise, add comments only for non-obvious behavior.

[Context: Logging]

What logging library should I use?

[Assistant]: Popular options include Winston, Pino, Bunyan...

[User]: Pino. Fastest, JSON by default, minimal API. Winston is bloated. I just need structured logs to stdout.

pino@^8.17.0
Reason: Fast structured logging

feat: add request logging middleware
Files: src/middleware/logging.ts
+23 -0

[Context: Error messages]

How detailed should error messages be?

[Assistant]: Balance between helpful and secure...

[User]: Different for dev and prod. Dev: full stack traces. Prod: error codes with correlation IDs. Never leak internals to users.

feat: add error response formatting with correlation IDs
Files: src/middleware/error-handler.ts, src/types/api-error.ts
+56 -12

PR: PR #28 - Add global exception handler [approve_with_changes]
Good. But rename 'handleException' to 'handleError'. Exceptions are a Java concept. In JS we handle errors.

[Context: Function length]

How long should a function be?

[Assistant]: Some say under 20 lines, others focus on single responsibility...

[User]: No magic number. A function should do one thing. If I can't name it clearly, it's doing too much. If it needs comments explaining sections, split it.

refactor: split large registration handler into steps
Files: src/handlers/register.ts
+45 -38

[Context: DRY principle]

I have similar code in two places. Should I extract it?

[Assistant]: DRY suggests yes...

[User]: Not yet. Duplication is cheaper than the wrong abstraction. Wait until I see it three times and understand the pattern.

PR: PR #31 - Extract common validation logic [reject]
These validations are only 'similar', not identical. Different contexts, different requirements. Keep them separate until they truly converge.

feat: add password reset flow
Files: src/handlers/reset-password.ts, src/email/templates.ts
+112 -0

[Context: Email templates]

Should I use a template engine for emails?

[Assistant]: Options include Handlebars, EJS, or React Email...

[User]: Template literals for now. Only 2 email types. I'll add React Email if we get to 10+ templates.

File: biome.json
Change: Migrated from ESLint+Prettier to Biome
Reason: Single tool, faster, same results

[Context: API versioning]

How should I version my API?

[Assistant]: Common approaches include URL path, header, query param...

[User]: URL path (/v1/). Clear, cacheable, obvious. Header versioning is clever but clients hate it.

refactor: add /v1 prefix to all routes
Files: src/routes/index.ts
+15 -12

PR: PR #36 - Add GraphQL endpoint [reject]
Why GraphQL? We have 5 REST endpoints. GraphQL adds complexity with no benefit at this scale. Solve problems you have, not problems you imagine.

[Context: Dependency injection]

Should I use a DI container?

[Assistant]: DI containers like tsyringe, inversify...

[User]: No container needed. Just pass dependencies as function arguments. If that gets unwieldy, I'll reconsider. Most DI libraries are overkill for non-enterprise apps.

feat: add rate limiting middleware
Files: src/middleware/rate-limit.ts
+34 -0

[Context: Rate limiting]

Redis or in-memory for rate limiting?

[Assistant]: Redis for distributed, in-memory for single instance...

[User]: In-memory. Single instance for now. I'll add Redis when we scale horizontally. YAGNI until then.

PR: PR #40 - Add Redis caching layer [reject]
We're not at scale where this matters. Add it when response times are actually a problem. Premature caching creates invalidation bugs.

test: add load tests with k6
Files: tests/load/registration.js
+45 -0

[Context: Performance testing]

When should I run load tests?

[Assistant]: Regular intervals, before major releases...

[User]: Before production and after major changes. Not in CI for every commit - too slow. Have a separate performance pipeline.

feat: add health check endpoint
Files: src/routes/health.ts
+23 -0

[Context: Health checks]

What should a health check include?

[Assistant]: Options include simple ping, database check, dependency checks...

[User]: Two endpoints: /health (always 200, for LB), /health/deep (checks DB, for monitoring). Separate concerns.

PR: PR #45 - Add Docker support [approve_with_changes]
Good Dockerfile. But remove the dev dependencies from the image. Production images should be minimal.

chore: optimize Docker image with multi-stage build
Files: Dockerfile
+25 -15

[Context: Environment config]

How should I handle environment variables?

[Assistant]: Use .env files, config libraries like dotenv...

[User]: Validate at startup with zod. If required config is missing, fail fast with clear error. Don't let the app start in bad state.

feat: add config validation on startup
Files: src/config/index.ts, src/config/schema.ts
+56 -12

[Context: Async patterns]

Callbacks, promises, or async/await?

[Assistant]: Modern JS favors async/await...

[User]: async/await everywhere. Promises when composing. Never callbacks unless forced by old library. Consistency is key.

PR: PR #50 - Refactor to use callbacks for performance [reject]
The performance difference is nanoseconds. Readability matters more. Keep async/await unless you profile and prove it's a bottleneck.

feat: add database migrations
Files: migrations/001_users.sql, src/db/migrate.ts
+78 -0

[Context: Migrations]

What migration tool should I use?

[Assistant]: Options include Knex migrations, Prisma migrate...

[User]: Plain SQL files with a simple runner. I want to see and version the exact DDL. Migration tools add magic.

PR: PR #53 - Add transaction support [approve_with_changes]
Good. But wrap the transaction logic in a helper that handles begin/commit/rollback. Reduces boilerplate.

refactor: add transaction helper function
Files: src/db/transaction.ts
+34 -0

[Context: Type assertions]

When is it okay to use 'as' type assertions?

[Assistant]: When you know more than the compiler...

[User]: Almost never. If I need 'as', usually means I should fix the types. Only exception: test mocks where I'm intentionally partial.

File: tsconfig.json
Change: Added noUncheckedIndexedAccess: true
Reason: Arrays should be checked before access. Prevents undefined bugs.

feat: add user profile endpoints
Files: src/handlers/profile.ts, src/routes/profile.ts
+89 -0

[Context: REST naming]

Singular or plural for REST resources?

[Assistant]: Both conventions exist...

[User]: Plural. /users, /posts, /comments. Consistent and matches the collection concept. Exception: /me for current user.

PR: PR #58 - Add soft deletes [needs_discussion]
Soft deletes add complexity. Do we actually need to restore data? If yes, proceed. If 'maybe someday', just delete. We have backups.

[Context: Soft vs hard delete]

Should I implement soft deletes?

[Assistant]: Soft deletes preserve data...

[User]: Only for things with legal/compliance requirements. For user data, yes. For temporary resources like sessions, hard delete.

feat: add soft delete for users with audit trail
Files: src/db/queries/users.ts, migrations/002_soft_delete.sql
+45 -12

[Context: Interface vs Type]

Should I use interface or type in TypeScript?

[Assistant]: Interfaces are extendable, types are more flexible...

[User]: type for data shapes, interface for contracts that might be implemented. In practice, type for almost everything.

PR: PR #62 - Use interfaces everywhere [reject]
Not needed. Types are fine for DTOs and response shapes. Save interfaces for when you need declaration merging or class contracts.

feat: add pagination to list endpoints
Files: src/handlers/users-list.ts, src/types/pagination.ts
+67 -12

[Context: Pagination style]

Offset or cursor pagination?

[Assistant]: Offset is simpler, cursor is more efficient for large datasets...

[User]: Cursor. Offset breaks on real-time data and gets slow at scale. Start with cursor, never have to migrate later.

refactor: switch to cursor-based pagination
Files: src/handlers/users-list.ts, src/types/pagination.ts
+45 -34

PR: PR #65 - Add OpenAPI spec [approve_with_changes]
Good idea. But generate from code, don't manually maintain. Code is source of truth. Spec should be derived.

@asteasolutions/zod-to-openapi@^5.0.0
Reason: Generate OpenAPI from Zod schemas

[Context: Documentation]

How should I document the API?

[Assistant]: OpenAPI/Swagger, README, dedicated docs site...

[User]: Generate OpenAPI from schemas. Self-documenting. Manual docs drift from reality. If the schema changes, docs update automatically.

feat: auto-generate OpenAPI spec from Zod schemas
Files: src/docs/openapi.ts, scripts/generate-docs.ts
+89 -0

[Context: Feature flags]

Should I add feature flags?

[Assistant]: Feature flags enable gradual rollouts...

[User]: Not until we have a feature that needs gradual rollout. Environment-based config suffices for now. Feature flags are infrastructure debt.

PR: PR #70 - Add LaunchDarkly integration [reject]
We're 3 developers. Talk to each other. Feature flags solve coordination problems at scale we don't have.

feat: add webhook support for user events
Files: src/webhooks/dispatcher.ts, src/types/events.ts
+78 -0

[Context: Event-driven]

Should I use an event bus like RabbitMQ?

[Assistant]: Event buses enable decoupling...

[User]: HTTP webhooks first. Simpler, debuggable, no infrastructure. Event bus when we have multiple consumers or need guaranteed delivery.

PR: PR #73 - Add microservices structure [reject]
We have one service with 10 endpoints. Microservices solve distribution problems. We have a complexity problem. Monolith first.

[Context: Monolith vs microservices]

When should we move to microservices?

[Assistant]: Common triggers include team scaling...

[User]: When team boundaries require service boundaries. Or when a component needs different scaling/deployment. Never for 'good architecture' alone.

refactor: organize monolith by feature, not layer
Files: src/features/users/*, src/features/auth/*
+0 -0
Note: File reorganization

[Context: Code organization]

Should I organize by layer (routes, handlers, models) or by feature?

[Assistant]: Both have merits...

[User]: Feature. When I work on users, I want all user code together. Layer organization means jumping between folders constantly.

PR: PR #77 - Add shared utils folder [reject]
What's 'shared'? If it's used everywhere, it's a library. If it's used by 2 features, put it in one and import. 'Shared' folders become junk drawers.

refactor: move truly shared code to lib/
Files: src/lib/result.ts, src/lib/validation.ts
+12 -8

[Context: Observability]

What observability stack do you recommend?

[Assistant]: Options include Datadog, New Relic, open-source stacks...

[User]: Logs, metrics, traces. Start with structured logs (Pino). Add Prometheus metrics when we need dashboards. Traces when debugging distributed calls.

feat: add prometheus metrics endpoint
Files: src/metrics/index.ts, src/routes/metrics.ts
+56 -0

PR: PR #80 - Add comprehensive metrics [approve_with_changes]
Too many metrics. Focus on RED: Rate, Errors, Duration. Add others when we have specific questions to answer.

[Context: Security headers]

What security headers should I add?

[Assistant]: Common headers include CORS, CSP, HSTS...

[User]: Use Helmet.js but understand each header. Don't just copy defaults. CSP needs to match actual resources we load.

helmet@^7.1.0
Reason: Security headers middleware

feat: add security headers with customized CSP
Files: src/middleware/security.ts
+34 -0

[Context: Code coverage]

What code coverage should I target?

[Assistant]: Industry standards suggest 80%...

[User]: Coverage is vanity. Focus on testing behavior, not lines. 100% coverage with bad tests is worse than 60% with good ones.

PR: PR #84 - Add tests to reach 80% coverage [approve_with_changes]
Some of these tests just exercise code without asserting behavior. Remove the getter tests. Add tests for edge cases we missed.

test: add edge case tests, remove trivial coverage tests
Files: tests/integration/auth.test.ts
+45 -23

[Context: Mocking]

When should I mock in tests?

[Assistant]: Mock external dependencies...

[User]: Mock what you don't own: external APIs, databases in unit tests. Never mock your own code - that tests implementation, not behavior.

PR: PR #87 - Mock database in handler tests [reject]
These are integration tests. Use a real test database. Mocking the DB defeats the purpose - we want to test actual queries.

chore: add test database setup with docker-compose
Files: docker-compose.test.yml, scripts/setup-test-db.sh
+45 -0

[Context: CI/CD]

GitHub Actions or CircleCI?

[Assistant]: Both are capable...

[User]: GitHub Actions. We're on GitHub, native integration, good enough for our needs. Simpler than managing another service.

ci: add GitHub Actions workflow
Files: .github/workflows/ci.yml
+56 -0

PR: PR #90 - Add deployment workflow [approve_with_changes]
Good start. But separate build and deploy stages. Build artifact should be immutable - same artifact to staging and production.

[Context: Deployment]

Kubernetes or simpler?

[Assistant]: K8s is powerful but complex...

[User]: Fly.io or Railway. We're a small app. K8s operational overhead doesn't make sense until we have dedicated infra team.

chore: add fly.io configuration
Files: fly.toml
+23 -0

[Context: Branch strategy]

GitFlow or trunk-based?

[Assistant]: GitFlow for releases, trunk-based for continuous...

[User]: Trunk-based. Short-lived feature branches, direct to main. GitFlow is for enterprises with release trains. We ship continuously.

PR: PR #93 - Add develop branch [reject]
We don't need develop. Main is always deployable. Feature branches merge to main. Adding branches adds ceremony, not safety.

[Context: PR reviews]

How thorough should code reviews be?

[Assistant]: Balance between thoroughness and velocity...

[User]: Focus on: logic errors, security issues, unclear code. Don't bikeshed naming or style - that's what linters are for. Ship fast, fix forward.

feat: add admin endpoints with role-based access
Files: src/features/admin/*, src/middleware/authorize.ts
+134 -0

[Context: Authorization]

RBAC or ABAC?

[Assistant]: RBAC is simpler, ABAC more flexible...

[User]: RBAC for now. We have 3 roles. ABAC adds complexity we don't need. Can migrate if requirements grow.

PR: PR #96 - Add CASL for authorization [reject]
CASL is overkill for 3 roles. A simple middleware checking role is enough. Libraries solve problems, not check boxes.

feat: add simple role-based middleware
Files: src/middleware/authorize.ts
+23 -0

[Context: Date handling]

date-fns or dayjs?

[Assistant]: Both are good, date-fns is tree-shakeable...

[User]: date-fns. Tree-shaking matters for bundle. Only import functions I use. dayjs requires full library.

date-fns@^3.3.0
Reason: Tree-shakeable date utilities

PR: PR #99 - Add moment.js for dates [reject]
Moment is deprecated and huge. Use date-fns or native Intl. Stop adding legacy libraries.

[Context: Null vs undefined]

Should I use null or undefined?

[Assistant]: JavaScript has both...

[User]: undefined for absence, null for intentional empty. In practice: avoid both with proper types. Optional chaining and nullish coalescing help.

refactor: replace null checks with optional chaining
Files: src/features/users/*
+15 -23

PR: PR #102 - Add utility functions for null checks [reject]
TypeScript has optional chaining and nullish coalescing. Native features > utility functions.

[Context: Project retrospective]

What would you change about this project?

[Assistant]: Looking at the codebase...

[User]: Started about right. Kept it simple, added complexity only when needed. Main regret: should have added cursor pagination earlier. Retrofitting was painful.

[Context: Learning patterns]

I keep making the same abstraction mistake. How do I learn?

[Assistant]: Practice and reflection...

[User]: The pattern: I want to 'do it right' so I abstract early. Then requirements change and abstraction doesn't fit. Lesson: write the thing three times, then extract.

[Context: Dealing with legacy code]

We have some legacy code from before I joined. Rewrite or refactor?

[Assistant]: Depends on the scope and risk...

[User]: Strangle fig pattern. Add tests first. Replace piece by piece. Big rewrites fail. Incremental improvement wins.

PR: PR #48 - Rewrite auth module [reject]
This is a full rewrite with no tests. Add integration tests first to capture current behavior. Then refactor with safety net.

[Context: Technical debt]

How do you manage technical debt?

[Assistant]: Track it, prioritize...

[User]: TODO comments for small stuff. Issues for bigger stuff. But most importantly: fix it when you're in the file. Don't plan debt cleanup sprints.

[Context: Team standards]

How do you establish coding standards in a team?

[Assistant]: Document and enforce...

[User]: Automate everything possible. Linters for style, types for correctness. Discussions for design patterns. Never argue about things a tool can check.

PR: PR #86 - Add style guide document [approve_with_changes]
Good initiative, but most of this is enforceable by biome. Convert to rules, not prose. Docs get ignored, linter errors don't.

chore: add strict biome rules replacing style guide
Files: biome.json
+34 -0

[Context: Project summary]

Looking back at 3 months, what are my main patterns?

[Assistant]: Analyzing your history...

[User]: Simplicity over cleverness. Types over tests (both matter, types catch more). Explicit over implicit. Native over library when possible. Ship, then improve.

PR: PR #105 - Final Q1 improvements [approve]
Good quarter. Code is simpler than when we started. That's rare - usually codebases only grow complex. Well done team.

docs: update README with current architecture
Files: README.md
+89 -45

[Context: Naming variables]

Best practices for variable naming?

[Assistant]: Be descriptive, use consistent conventions...

[User]: Names should explain what, not how. 'filteredUsers' good, 'loopResult' bad. If I need a comment to explain a name, the name is wrong.

PR: PR #24 - Rename variables for clarity [approve]
Good change. 'data' -> 'userProfile', 'res' -> 'apiResponse'. Specific is always better than generic.

[Context: Boolean naming]

How should I name boolean variables?

[Assistant]: Use prefixes like is, has, should...

[User]: is/has/can/should prefix for booleans. 'active' is ambiguous. 'isActive' is clear. Exception: obvious booleans like 'visible', 'enabled'.

refactor: standardize boolean naming with is/has prefixes
Files: src/types/user.ts, src/handlers/profile.ts
+23 -23

[Context: Function naming]

What about function naming conventions?

[Assistant]: Verbs for actions, nouns for getters...

[User]: Verb for actions (createUser, deletePost), adjective for transformers (formatted, validated), question for predicates (isEmpty, hasAccess).

PR: PR #88 - Rename utility functions [approve]
Good. 'process' -> 'normalizeInput', 'handle' -> 'routeRequest'. Generic verbs are code smells.

[Context: Constants naming]

SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE for constants?

[Assistant]: It's common in some languages...

[User]: Only for true constants: MAX_RETRIES, API_TIMEOUT. Not for config values that could change. Regular camelCase for those.

refactor: fix constant naming conventions
Files: src/config/constants.ts
+12 -12

[Context: Import organization]

How should I organize imports?

[Assistant]: Group by type, alphabetize...

[User]: External packages first, then internal. Let the linter sort within groups. Don't waste mental energy on import order.

File: biome.json
Change: Added import sorting rules
Reason: Automate import organization

PR: PR #71 - Manual import sorting [reject]
Remove manual import organization. Enable biome's import sorter. Never manually do what tools can automate.

[Context: Early returns]

Should I use early returns or single return?

[Assistant]: Both have advocates...

[User]: Early returns always. Guard clauses at the top, happy path at the bottom. Deeply nested if/else is unreadable.

refactor: convert nested conditions to early returns
Files: src/handlers/register.ts, src/handlers/login.ts
+25 -35

PR: PR #42 - Add else blocks for clarity [reject]
This adds visual noise. After 'if (invalid) return error', the next line is implicitly the valid case. No else needed.

[Context: Ternary operators]

When are ternary operators okay?

[Assistant]: For simple conditionals...

[User]: Single line, simple values only. condition ? valueA : valueB. Never nested ternaries. If it needs multiple lines, use if/else.

PR: PR #94 - Refactor with ternaries [approve_with_changes]
The nested ternary on line 45 is unreadable. Convert to if/else or early returns. Clever code is not good code.

[Context: Destructuring]

Best practices for destructuring?

[Assistant]: Use for objects and arrays...

[User]: Destructure at point of use, not at function start. Only destructure what you need. Deep destructuring is a smell - flatten your data.

PR: PR #61 - Destructure all params at start [reject]
This destructures 12 fields, uses 3. Only destructure what you need, where you need it.

refactor: clean up excessive destructuring
Files: src/features/users/handlers.ts
+8 -15

[Context: Spread operator]

When to use spread vs Object.assign?

[Assistant]: Spread is more readable...

[User]: Spread for shallow copies: { ...obj, newProp }. Object.assign only for mutating in place, which I avoid anyway. Immutability by default.

PR: PR #41 - Use Object.assign for merging [reject]
Use spread: { ...defaults, ...overrides }. Clearer than Object.assign, same result, immutable.

[Context: Final thoughts]

Any advice for developers starting out?

[Assistant]: Learn fundamentals, practice...

[User]: Write code. Delete code. Shipping beats planning. Types catch bugs, tests verify behavior. Simple code lives longer. The best code is code you don't write.

chore: Q1 complete - tag v1.0.0
Files: package.json
+1 -1

PR: PR #106 - v1.0.0 release [approve]
From 0 to production in 3 months. Clean code, comprehensive tests, simple architecture. This is how software should be built. Ship it.

[Context: Project complete]

v1.0 is live. What's the most important thing I learned?

[Assistant]: Reflecting on your journey...

[User]: Simplicity is a feature. Every line of code is a liability. The goal isn't to write code, it's to solve problems. Sometimes the best solution is not writing code at all.
